title: 3Sum
statement:
Given an integer array `nums`, return all the triplets `[nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]]` such that `i != j`, `i != k`, `j != k`, and `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0`.

The solution set must not contain duplicate triplets.

This is one of the most frequently asked medium-difficulty interview problems. The classic approach combines sorting with the two-pointer technique to achieve O(n^2) time instead of O(n^3).

examples.explanation: Two distinct triplets sum to zero.
The only triplet sums to zero.

editorial.approach: First sort the array (O(n log n)). Then for each index `i` (skipping duplicates), use two pointers — `left = i + 1` and `right = nums.length - 1` — to find pairs that sum to `-nums[i]`. If the sum is too low, advance `left`; if too high, retreat `right`. When a match is found, record the triplet and skip any duplicate values on both sides before continuing. The sorting step enables both the two-pointer search and the deduplication logic.
editorial.complexity: O(n^2) time / O(log n) to O(n) space depending on sorting implementation
